nodes.name: SILAR Deposition of FeNi Vanadate
nodes.procedure: FeNi(VO4)x@NF was synthesized by successive ionic layer adsorption and reaction (SILAR) method through 30 sequential cycles at room temperature. Each SILAR cycle consists of four steps: (i) adsorption of Fe3+ and Ni2+ cations from aqueous solution (pH=2.6, Fe:Ni=1:1) and vanadate anions (pH=12.3) as ionic layers over NF; (ii) etching excessive ionic species through alternating dip-coating; (iii) ionic reaction between adsorbed Fe, Ni, and vanadate species; (iv) deposition of FeNi-vanadate nanoparticles. The reaction follows: 2FeCl3·6H2O + 4NiCl2 + (3+x)Na3VO4·2H2O → FeVO4 + Ni3(VO4)2 + FeNi(VO4)x + byproducts. The pH difference between metal (2.6) and vanadate (12.3) solutions etches unreacted precipitates while leaving nanoparticles on NF. Fe:Ni:V mole ratio in baths is 1:1:2.

unit_operations.name: Ionic Layer Adsorption
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: i) Adsorption of Fe/Ni cations and vanadate anions as an ionic layer over NF.

unit_operations.name: Etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: ii) Etching the excessive ionic species through alternating dip-coating.

unit_operations.name: Ionic Reaction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: iii) Ionic reaction between Fe, Ni, and vanadate species.

unit_operations.name: Nanoparticle Deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: iv) Deposition of FeNi-(binuclear) vanadate nanoparticles through sequential SILAR cycles.

nodes.source_text: The electrode is prepared via the SILAR process... Through the sequential SILAR cycles, nanoparticles form successively. The following reaction betides... 2 FeCl3·6H2O + 4 NiCl2 + (3 + x) Na3VO4·2H2O → FeVO4 + Ni3(VO4)2 + FeNi(VO4)x...

nodes.name: FeNi Hydroxide Deposition
nodes.procedure: Unmodified FeNi catalyst prepared by alternating dip-coating into cationic bath (FeCl3·6H2O + NiCl2) without vanadate, producing nanosheets on NF.
nodes.source_text: SILAR did not occur for the unmodified FeNi and only alternating dip-coating into cationic bath produced the nanosheets.

nodes.name: FeVO4 Deposition
nodes.procedure: Single metallic vanadate FeVO4@NF prepared by SILAR process similar to main catalyst but using only Fe and vanadate precursors.
nodes.source_text: Single metallic vanadates, FeVO4 and Ni3(VO4)2, were also prepared for comparison.

nodes.name: Ni3(VO4)2 Deposition
nodes.procedure: Single metallic vanadate Ni3(VO4)2@NF prepared by SILAR process similar to main catalyst but using only Ni and vanadate precursors.
nodes.source_text: Single metallic vanadates, FeVO4 and Ni3(VO4)2, were also prepared for comparison.

nodes.characterization_summary: GIXRD patterns show that both FeNi(VO4)x@NF and FeNi@NF are amorphous with poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SILAR-deposited FeNi(VO4)x and dip-coated FeNi catalysts are amorphous (grazing incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) patterns, Figure 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM reveals uniformly distributed nanoparticles forming a film with void space on FeNi(VO4)x@NF, contrasting with ultrathin nanosheets on FeNi@NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FeNi(VO4)x@NF has uniformly distributed nanoparticles over the smooth surface of the NF network (Figure 1b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows nanoscaled interconnected porous film of FeNi(VO4)x nanoparticles on NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nanoscaled growth of FeNi(VO4)x nanoparticles is revealed by high-angle annular dark-field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM, Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM-EDS confirms uniform elemental distribution of Fe, Ni, V, O in FeNi(VO4)x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The successful vanadate modification of Fe and Ni species is demonstrated by the uniform elemental distribution in FeNi(VO4)x (Figure 1e-h).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM and SAED confirm amorphous structure of FeNi(VO4)x with no clear lattice fringes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No clear and indexed lattice fringes are visible in the catalyst grains, confirming the amorphous structure (HRTEM and selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern Figure 1i).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 856.3 eV (2p3/2) and 873.9 eV (2p1/2) indicating Ni between 2+ and 3+, Fe 2p peaks at 711.5 eV (2p3/2) and 724.6 eV (2p1/2) indicating Fe3+, V 2p doublets at 517.4/524.8 eV (V5+) and 516.8/524.0 eV (V4+).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The recorded peaks in the high-resolution core-level spectra, around 856.3 and 873.9 eV in Ni 2p region... V 2p region demonstrates doublets featured at 5174, 524.8 and 516.8, 524.0 eV corresponding to V 2p3/2 and V 2p1/2 configurations of V5+ and V4+, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows intensified Ni-O (450-550 cm⁻¹) and Fe-O (600-700 cm⁻¹) bands in FeNi(VO4)x@NF vs FeNi@NF, and vanadate V-O bands at 338 cm⁻¹, 750-950 cm⁻¹ with Γ1 at 821 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The chemical structure is characterized by Raman shifts of the as-prepared catalysts... The observed characteristic vibrations comply with FeNi-mixed vanadates as the chemical structure of the catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA evaluated from double-layer capacitance Cdl shows vanadate modification enlarges ECSA and surface roughness factor RF of FeNi(VO4)x@NF compared to controls.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA values were evaluated based on electrochemical double-layer capacitance (C_DL) (Electronic Supporting Information and Figure S27, Supporting Information).
